Theme

Latin word

mōrālis

mōrālis, mōrāle

adjective, third declension

moral, concerning conduct

In this lexicon

  • moral

    the recommended word · classical · Cic. Fat. 1: sed decet augentem linguam Latīnam nōmināre mōrālem (Lewis & Short); Sen. Ep. 89.9; Quint. 12.2.10 (Lewis & Short)

Examples

  • quia pertinet ad mōrēs, quōs ἤθη Graecī vocant, nōs eam partem philosophiae dē mōribus appellāre solēmus; sed decet augentem linguam Latīnam nōmināre mōrālem

    because it concerns conduct, which the Greeks call ēthē, we usually call that part of philosophy “on conduct”; but in enriching the Latin language it is fitting to call it “moral”Cic. Fat. 1 (Lewis & Short)

    In the entry for moral

  • philosophiae trēs partēs esse dīxērunt, mōrālem, nātūrālem, et ratiōnālem

    they said that philosophy has three parts, the moral, the natural and the rationalSen. Ep. 89.9 (Lewis & Short)
